items.text: Team reviewed prototype specs: kinetic charger, standard chip, soft rubber case, fruit-inspired designs, and potential voice recognition. Discussed clam-shell design, screen placement, and remote functionality.
Industrial Designer presented exterior: plastic body with neutral color options, wide choice of patterns, and customizable rubberized casing. Confirmed clam-shell structure with inset top screen.
Internal specs include kinetic batteries, black and white touch screen, and standard buttons (volume, channel, power). Logo placement options debated: bezzled, inset, or engraved.

Remote control features discussed: voice recognition to locate remote, standard TV transmission via infrared. Infrared sender position finalized on front layer for signal transmission when device is open.
Voice recognition system availability and cost remain uncertain; team noted it might be for next time. Infrared transmission confirmed as standard method using same medium as all TVs.
Top screen to contain all remote functions; bottom screen for standard buttons. Logo placement on top screen decided to avoid interfering with product look when closed.
Industrial Designer and User Interface Designer collaborated on prototype. Industrial Designer will show presentation; User Interface Designer to hold device. Evaluation criteria prepared for review.

The team evaluates a remote control prototype against criteria from market research, including look, innovation, usability, and design features like spongy texture and fruit/vegetable colors, using a seven point scale for consensus ratings.
The team discusses specific criteria such as minimizing R_S_I_, voice recognition, and beeper functions, noting ambivalence about voice recognition and considering a beeper as a sideline option.

The Marketing Expert will lead the evaluation by presenting criteria, collecting individual ratings from all team members on a whiteboard, calculating averages, and handling decimal rounding to one place.
The team rates the fancy look and feel criterion, with individual scores ranging from two to four, resulting in an average of two and three quarters.

The team rates the technologically innovative criterion, with the Industrial Designer initially giving a one, the Project Manager a two, and the User Interface Designer correcting their initial rating to two, averaging to two point five.
The team rates the ease of use criterion, with most members agreeing on a rating of two, though the Marketing Expert initially suggested one before adjusting for arithmetic ease.

Regarding incorporates current fashion trends, the team clarifies that the prototype's base is white or light blue with customizable faces, allowing for strong fruit and vegetable colors, leading to a consensus rating of one.

The team evaluates design criteria including RSI minimization, voice recognition feasibility, and cost. They review a prototype's specifications, correct errors in the electronics count and curve type, and finalize material ratings before approving the prototype for production.

The team discusses the feasibility of voice recognition and its cost, noting it is feasible but may require volume adjustment features. They agree on a rating of one for this criterion based on current technology limitations.

The team decides to proceed with producing the prototype and marketing it, as the evaluation findings show high ratings for most criteria and current technology limits further RSI minimization improvements.
The Project Manager instructs the User Interface Designer to unplug the screen. The team confirms they are still on for the 'kinetic' project.

The team corrects the electronics specification, changing the number of kinetic cells from three to one and clarifying the chip configuration involves one double-curved chip, one sample sensor, and one sample speaker.
The team finalizes the material composition for the casing, agreeing on one plastic component and assigning a rating of point five to the rubber component used as a casing to prevent rolling.

The team discusses material costs for a remote control, confirming the case is rubber, not plastic, and debating whether to include the extra rubber cost in the total price or as a separate line item.
Participants evaluate design changes, including switching from a kinetic battery to a standard battery and removing voice recognition, analyzing the impact on total cost and customer appeal.

The team reviewed the project budget, confirming costs are under the limit. They discussed team dynamics, noting strong collaboration and creativity, though voice recognition was excluded from the final design.
The group evaluated communication tools used during the project, agreeing that while adequate, more time and separation might have improved the use of the outer email system.
Participants discussed remote control design, observing that companies focus on the main device rather than the remote, but acknowledged a desire for unique, custom-made plastic remotes.
The team asked how to evaluate the materials used for communicating and sharing information, and whether those materials could have been better or more adequate.
The team discusses market research showing consumers prefer familiar phone models over new innovations, noting that current product changes are driven by profit motives rather than user needs.

The project is evaluated as successful for staying within budget and creating an innovative item, though the team acknowledges the final product may not be manufactured due to high costs or lack of market fit.

The Project Manager notes that the current budget covers only production costs, excluding overheads like salaries and heating, suggesting a potential need for a new project team to address future pricing and cash flow issues.
The Project Manager will delegate tasks in their role as Project Supervisor to catch up on missed work, with approximately fifty minutes remaining in the meeting.
The team will complete a final questionnaire regarding the meeting and the celebration, which may involve a twenty-five pound reward or dancing on desks.
The team questions whether the current budget includes all costs such as overheads and building heating, and discusses the possibility of evaluating team influence in future meetings.
